journey.name: TL-19 A task created under an active query is brought into view
journey.description:
REGRESSION GUARD. This journey used to assert the defect: the query lived in the list state and nothing cleared it on the way back from a save, so a new task whose title did not match the live filter was created, cached, and invisible. The user saw the editor close - the app's only signal that a save worked - and then a list that said "No tasks match ...", which is the same picture a failed save paints. Filed as issue #16 and now fixed: the editor reports a successful save back to the list, which clears the query so the task the user just typed is on screen.
A search field is the most likely place to arrive from: typing a title, finding it is not there, and tapping plus is a normal way to add a task.
The result is consumed once, so a query typed after the save is left alone. That is asserted at the end rather than left to the unit test, because the wiring runs through the back stack.
Preconditions: adb shell am force-stop com.rounds.test.to_dolist adb shell am start -n com.rounds.test.to_dolist/.MainActivity --es qa_failure_rate 0.0

actions.action: Type "invoice" into the "Search by title" field
Verify that the text “No tasks match “invoice”.” is on screen
Tap the element with the content description "Add task"
Verify that the app returns to the "Tasks" screen
Verify that the "Search by title" field is empty
Verify that "Bought milk" is on screen
Verify that "Bought milk" is the last row in the list
Verify that all four seed rows are on screen as well
Type "invoice" into the "Search by title" field again
Verify that the text “No tasks match “invoice”.” is on screen, so the save result was consumed and does not clear a later query
